x: During the past months we were fortunate in securing the services of of a Continental coach, Herr Franz Stampfl, whose vivacious enthusiasm and expert knowledge soon endeared him to our members ....

In 1952 we had the temporary assistance of FRANZ STAMPFL (as we had done briefly in pre-War years) as a professional coach. Franz, who had been a member of the Austrian Olympic team and now holds a University post in Australia, combined knowledge with terrific vitality and enthusiasm.
To build them up again he began to run regularly at Battersea Park track and there, of course, he soon met members of Belgrave Harriers and in particular the renowned athletic coach Franz Stampfl.
Television viewers who watched "The African Runners" in the Olympic Games series saw a face familiar to us in the early fifties - Franz Stampfl.
Athletic Clubs were keen to get going again after the war, and, although not eligible for membership we engaged a professional coach Franz Stampfl, who had represented Austria in the Javelin.

Our members who were active in the period just before and after the war were only too well aware that another page of athletic history was turned earlier this year when on March 19th Franz Stampfl passed away in Melbourne, Australia.

(Little did we know how honoured we were to receive advice from Franz Stampfl, Frank Simmons, Bert Footer, Frank Elson and others wearing their Club track suits with coloured flashes!) Fifty years on and the Duke of York's is due for demolition and redevelopment.
The sad news for the Club, and British athletics, was the departure for Australia of Franz Stampfl who had coached Club members since his arrival from Austria in 1937.
